items.note: REWORDED after measurement. The old wording said three ambiguities 'all reduce to the same missing datum -- which BLOCK the caret is in', and that turned out to be half right. items.title: finding 059: the engine judges an inline format by the document's state instead of core's `success` -- DONE, shipped 2026-08-19
items.source: finding 059, measured on the shipped v3 artifact 2026-08-17

The list actions use the same parameterised mechanism and still work, so the difference is this slot's argument name or type, not parameters in general. On v2 (before the fix) bold APPLIED and merely ignored `enabled` -- which is finding 045 -- so the fix turned a wrong-direction action into no action at all. BLOCKS the next link because shipping again without resolving it ships a build whose formatting buttons cannot be used. Two candidates, both needing native measurement FIRST: withdraw inlineFormatArgument (back to v2 behaviour, on-only), or find the argument form core accepts. Mechanism deliberately not named (040/048 precedent). MECHANISM ESTABLISHED same day by native control (findings/evidence/059/native/): the parameterised .uno:Bold DOES apply -- marker typed after `value:true` comes back fo:font-weight="bold", after `value:false` comes back normal -- while reporting success:false, wasModified:true. The bare form reports success:true and leaves the text NOT bold. The .uno:DefaultBullet control behaves the same way, which is why the barrier path (which does not gate on success) kept working. So DO NOT withdraw inlineFormatArgument: the fix is correct and the defect is commandResultSucceeded() at probe_engine.cpp:1696 requiring success:true, turned into LOK_COMMAND_FAILED at :2286. CANDIDATE PREDICATES, corrected 2026-08-18: the barrier's readback is the ONLY candidate left. wasModified is out, and by source rather than by measurement -- desktop/source/lib/init.cxx:5517-5518 passes pDocSh->IsModified() as a constructor argument to DispatchResultListener, i.e. captured BEFORE dispatchCommand() runs (the member's own comment at :5073 says 'modified before saving', and :5098 copies it out unchanged). It reports whether the document was already dirty, not whether this command changed anything, so it cannot separate an applied command from a refused one. MEASURED 2026-08-18 (findings/evidence/059/native/predicate/, ten arms, prediction committed first): all four slots apply correctly and all four broadcast .uno:<Slot>=true, so the readback IS available for all of them -- including underline and strikeout, whose absence of a state cache is justified in probe_engine.cpp:4308-4310 by a claim about GetKitUnoCommandList() that core's source contradicts. But the predicate must NOT be 'a broadcast arrived': core broadcasts a state CHANGE, so the value:false arms produced no broadcast at all while doing exactly the right thing. The predicate that survives is the barrier's existing one -- compare observed state against requested state (formatBarrierPostconditionMet, :1189). STILL OWED before this ships: a genuine negative arm. The intended refusal (setViewReadOnly) did not refuse -- core applied the command anyway -- so this round proved the predicate agrees, not that it can disagree. Also unmeasured: whether the state cache is primed when the predicate needs it (finding 021's shape). Superseded note follows: the readback was to be measured PER SLOT: bold, italic, underline and strikethrough are four different slots and the last two have no state cache. A refusal arm must use a command core knows but cannot run -- an unknown slot emits no LOK_CALLBACK_UNO_COMMAND_RESULT at all (comphelper/source/misc/dispatchcommand.cxx:48-50), so it would measure nothing. MEASURED 2026-08-18 (findings/evidence/059/wasm/): the WASM build DOES apply the command while reporting failure, for all four slots -- each arm's marker comes back carrying exactly the slot that was pressed, with a no-command control on the same fixture coming back unstyled. So the shipped product applies the user's formatting and then tells them the action failed and to return to a checkpoint: it asks them to discard work to undo a change that succeeded. That raises the cost of NOT fixing this and it is why this item blocks the link. Also measured: the range route is closed engine-side -- with the page's gesture mask lifted all four dispatches return EDITOR_FORMAT_GESTURE_UNSUPPORTED from editorGesturePermitted (probe_engine.cpp:4247-4252), which is the first RUNTIME witness for p1-2-gesture-mask-inherited. THE TWO THINGS OWED ARE NOW MEASURED (2026-08-19, findings/evidence/059/native/negative-arm/, nine arms, zero disagreements, analyzer self-test 10/10). (1) THE PREDICATE CAN SAY NO, on two arms, and it says no exactly where the document says no: a wrong argument TYPE ({"Bold":{"type":"string",...}}) leaves the text normal with no broadcast, and a paragraph inside a text:protected section refuses the dispatch and does not even take the typing. Asked four ways rather than one, because 037's lesson is that a guard may decline for another reason or not at all -- and setViewReadOnly, asked again, STILL does not refuse. (2) THE CACHE IS PRIMED, at document load, for all four slots including underline and strikeout, which contradicts probe_engine.cpp:4308 a second way (core's own source already did). But the priming comes from the LOAD broadcast, not from caret movement: moving between two paragraphs that share a state broadcasts nothing, so an engine that starts listening later is back in finding 021's shape and the implementation must not assume a gesture refreshes it. (3) NEW, and it sharpens why the current gate is wrong rather than merely weak: `success: true` appeared on exactly the two arms where core IGNORED the argument and toggled, and `success: false` on every arm where core honoured the parameterised form. The field commandResultSucceeded() gates on is ANTI-CORRELATED with the caller's request being honoured on this build. WHAT IS STILL OWED: the engine change itself, and the WASM half of this measurement -- nothing above describes the WASM build (040/048 precedent). THE ENGINE CHANGE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN ON 2026-08-19, and the reason is this finding's own history: 045's fix shipped with native evidence, a static check, a queue item and a link -- and nobody ever pressed the button, which is what 059 IS. Writing a second engine fix that cannot be exercised until the next link repeats that shape exactly. The half that was owed and blocking (the negative arm, the priming) is measured and committed; what remains is unblocked by evidence and gated only on the link, which is the user's decision. THE DESIGN, so whoever links has it: (a) `parseFormatStatePayload`'s booleanCommands list (probe_engine.cpp:1167) carries only Bold/Italic/DefaultBullet/DefaultNumbering -- Underline and Strikeout must be added there and in `updateEditorFormatState` (:1435); (b) the new state fields must go INSIDE the OXSDK_E2_FORMAT_BARRIER guard, NOT beside boldKnown/italicKnown which are unguarded -- the comment at :283 says why, E1-C validated the frozen e1-editor profiles at a specific WASM hash and an unguarded field silently changes what they emit; (c) the gate itself is at :2286, where `!commandResultSucceeded(payload)` becomes LOK_COMMAND_FAILED. For the four inline commands that call must consult the postcondition instead, under the name `inlineFormatArgumentResolved` so this item's sentinel flips visibly. TWO HAZARDS, both measured rather than anticipated: (1) DO NOT gate the inline postcondition on `formatStateStale`. It is set true by every caret move (:2177) and cleared only when a watched payload arrives (:1459) -- and the 2026-08-19 round measured that moving between two paragraphs that already share a state broadcasts NOTHING. So a stale-gated postcondition would refuse exactly the case where the document is already in the requested state, which is a correct outcome, not a failure. (2) The engine's own comment at :423-427 says the state broadcast cannot be the postcondition because core stays silent when nothing changed. That objection is about treating the broadcast as an EVENT and it stands. Comparing the cached STATE against the requested value is a different thing and does not have that problem: 'the command never arrived and the state was already right' and 'the command arrived and set it' both score met, and both are correct -- the postcondition holds either way. And both measure the RECOVERY MACHINE rather than the user's route INTO it, so they are a supplement, never a replacement. MEASURED 2026-08-21, and TWO corrections to this item's own text. (1) The debt is no longer hypothetical: on FIREFOX the 038 inducer ALREADY does not reproduce, so recovery-returns-what-the-product-promised is NOT_ESTABLISHED there today -- the coverage is already gone on one of two supported browsers. (2) 'both reachable through public API' is WRONG for the worker-termination candidate: _worker.terminate() is private and reached only inside restart()/dispose() (sdk/document-sdk.js:333), and it is not a selection gesture so it cannot satisfy the capability clause on recovery-returns-what-the-product-promised either. The short-timeoutMs candidate is also not reachable: the product constructs its session WITHOUT selectionTimeoutMs (web/e2-editor-app.js:762) so it defaults to 5000 (editor-session.js:84), and passing one would put test-only configuration into the product. A third candidate was tried -- a whole-canvas drag in a long dirty document, which needs no product change -- and did NOT reach recoverable-error at 40 or 200 pages. That arm is a WEAK elimination and says so: the reported latency is placeCaret's, not the selection readback's, so it does not establish that a range was selected at all. Do not escalate the page count until the probe has a positive control. Probe: tools/probe_second_recovery_inducer.py (diagnostic). Evidence: findings/evidence/queue-recovery-inducer-depends-on-an-unfixed-defect/RESULT.md. Nothing was wired into the regression net; the check still reports NOT_ESTABLISHED and names 038, so the loud exit is intact. URGENT AS OF 2026-08-27, AND NOT HYPOTHETICAL ANY MORE: the day this item feared has arrived on the accessibility lineage. `recovery-returns-what-the-product-promised` is NOT_ESTABLISHED on `e2-editor-v11` in 5 runs of 5 -- finding 038's drag no longer wedges that core -- while it PASSES on the shipped profile. The loud exit worked exactly as designed (the check names 038 rather than passing silently), but the consequence stands: on the profile a cutover would ship, the recovery path -- checkpoint plus 'return to your checkpoint', the product's safety net for unsaved work -- IS NOT COVERED BY ANYTHING. An adjudication on the cutover called this a finding wearing an NE costume, because the net counts NOT_ESTABLISHED as neither. FIRST CANDIDATE ATTEMPTED AND NOT LANDED, 2026-08-27: induce a REAL uncaught error inside the document worker over CDP, which is the failure class `DocumentSdk._handleCrash` listens for and needs no product change. Three things were established and one was not. (1) The worker cannot be found by URL: `Target.getTargets` reports eight `worker` targets with EMPTY urls, because the verified loader builds the worker from a blob and the wasm's pthreads each occupy a target. (2) Nothing addressed to an attached worker session is answered -- not `Runtime.evaluate` and not `Runtime.enable`, on all eight, from the page connection AND from a second connection to the browser endpoint. (3) The reason is NOT that the worker threads are blocked, which was the hypothesis: `Runtime.enable` is answered by the browser rather than by the target's JavaScript thread, and it times out too. That discriminator is the only reason a plausible and wrong conclusion ('pthreads sit in Atomics.wait, so they cannot be asked') was not written down as the answer. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: why the attached sessions are silent. The probe is at findings/evidence/queue-recovery-inducer-depends-on-an-unfixed-defect/. NEXT, and it is a DESIGN choice rather than a detail, so it belongs to the user: either keep digging at CDP, or take the item's second candidate (a deliberately short `timeoutMs`, TIMEOUT being in RECOVERY_ERRORS) which needs a seam the product does not currently expose, or accept the coverage gap and record it as a named limit of the accessibility lineage. DONE 2026-08-28. The second inducer is an uncaught error inside the DOCUMENT WORKER -- the failure class `DocumentSdk._handleCrash` listens for (document-sdk.js:126-129), depending on no upstream defect, needing no product change and no test-only affordance. Only the killing step is new: the checkpoint is already written by the selection gesture the arm performs (measured `有（r2）` on v11 even where 038 wedges nothing), so the branch under test is the same one 038's route exercises. MEASURED: on e2-editor-v11 the fallback fires, the session reaches recoverable-error, the checkpoint SURVIVES THE CRASH, the notice is offered and enabled on the `checkpoint` branch, saved and unsaved work both come back, and the arm PASSES -- the run goes 37/3 to 38 PASS / 2 NE. On the shipped profile the control is clean: 038 still reproduces, the fallback is never reached, nothing about that path changed. That closes the NE delta an adjudication had called a finding wearing an NE costume. THE ACCEPTANCE CONDITION CHANGED WITH IT, deliberately and with the reason written at the branch: NOT_ESTABLISHED used to mean '038 no longer reproduces' and now means 'no inducer could reach the state at all'; `finding038Reproduced` still records the fact about the core. THE LESSON, three times in one day: a thing that arrives as an EVENT gets thrown away by a reader written for request/response. items.title: finding 062's LAYER is established: the ENGINE returns an unpainted tile above 32,767 px and reports success
items.note: The wall is bracketed narrowly: with one document held fixed and devicePixelRatio swept, 32,590 px of canvas height draws and 32,889 px is blank, and 32,767 = 2^15-1 sits between them. It is NOT the canvas element's cap -- that was measured separately at 65,535 in both Chrome and Firefox, and 65,234 for Chrome at 2400 px wide -- so this is a 16-bit limit inside the render path. The same twenty-page document draws at devicePixelRatio 1 and is blank at 2, so it is a property of the document times the display, not of the document. blocksRelink is FALSE and that is not a judgement that this is unimportant: the first work owed is the experiment that says WHICH LAYER loses the pixels, and until that is done, declaring it engine-side would be the mistake findings 040 and 048 were filed against. THE EXPERIMENT: call document.render() through the shell with canvasHeightPx 32,590 and 32,889 and compare the returned width/height and pixel byte length. render() does not throw today and the product page publishes no session handle, which is why this cannot be answered from the product path. If the engine returns an empty tile this item becomes engine-side and blocksRelink must be flipped. ANSWERED 2026-08-19 (findings/evidence/062/layer/): THE PAGE SIDE, and no link is needed. Asked step by step on the shipped artifact, at heights straddling the wall. The engine's tile is correct at every height -- byte length exactly width x height x 4, dark pixels present, nothing thrown, including at 34,847 where the product is blank on the same document. ImageData builds from all of them. putImageData paints them, on a detached canvas and on one attached and CSS-sized like the product's. And the decisive one: with the PRODUCT sitting in its blank state, a block painted onto that same canvas by the harness lands 36,250 of 36,250 expected pixels while the product's own ink is one column. Same canvas, same size, same moment. So the canvas is fine, the engine is fine, and the product never put the tile there. WHICH page-side step is NOT established and is tracked separately as queue-long-document-blank-page-is-page-side. CORRECTED THE SAME DAY. The paragraph above said page side. It was wrong, and the way it was wrong is the reusable part: every probe run swept an ASCENDING LADDER of canvas heights inside ONE engine session, so the first render was always below the limit and painted, and the later over-limit arms came back carrying content -- which exonerated the engine. One render per page load, which is what the product actually does, returns an unpainted buffer every time. THE ANSWER IS THE ENGINE SIDE and the limit is exactly 2^15-1: at width 362, height 32,767 paints (41,762 dark pixels) and 32,768 does not, at the same 45.2 MB; at width 725, 32,767 paints and 34,847 does not. Two widths, buffers differing by a factor of two, the same height boundary -- so it is the HEIGHT, not the memory. The buffer is always exactly width x height x 4 bytes, ImageData always builds, and render() never throws. The three page-side steps were each measured and are each fine: the product's putImageData paints exactly the all-zero image it is handed (2,105,295 of 2,105,340 sampled pixels fully transparent), its blank canvas takes 36,250 of 36,250 pixels from the harness, and the paint request it sends is byte for byte the one the probe sends. WHY THIS STILL DOES NOT BLOCK THE LINK: nothing forces the product to ask for one tile as tall as the whole document. Rendering in strips no taller than 32,767 -- or using the TileScheduler editor-session.js already imports -- avoids the limit entirely and is a page-side change.

items.title: the engine reports the document's size on every paint, so a client can tell it grew -- DONE, shipped 2026-08-19
items.note: Measured through the product's own buttons: a two-page document opens at canvas height 2007, an insert of 3,336 characters leaves it at 2007, and saving those bytes and re-opening them gives 3002 -- exactly what a genuine three-page document reports. So the document grew by a page, the canvas did not, and nothing was said. It fires at two pages: there is no length threshold. WHY THIS ONE IS NOT PAGE-SIDE, unlike the blank-page half: `DocumentHandle.heightTwips` is assigned once from the open metadata (sdk/document-sdk.js:374), the engine calls getDocumentSize exactly once, at open (probe_engine.cpp:2520), and no SDK operation re-reads it -- the operations are open, paint, click, insertText, search, getSelection, replaceSelection, undo, save, comments, tracked changes, and none of them reports a size. So the page has no way to learn the document is taller, and `document-invalidated` calling layoutCanvas() would not help: it would recompute from the same stale number. THE FIX is engine-side and small -- report the document size on the paint result, or add an operation for it -- and it therefore has to ride a link. blocksRelink is TRUE because the fix cannot happen without one and shipping again without it ships an editor whose page count is frozen at the moment the file was opened. , artifact 296f3ea727725fbb. handlePaintTile now re-reads getDocumentSize and puts documentWidthTwips / documentHeightTwips / documentSizeChanged on the reply; the worker forwards them (its reply is a WHITELIST, so the engine change alone would have been invisible -- worth remembering); DocumentHandle.render() keeps the handle current; and the page re-layouts and repaints when the size changed. Guarded by OXSDK_E2_FORMAT_BARRIER: every profile shares handlePaintTile and the frozen ones were validated at a specific reply shape.
items.checkNote: Present now.

items.title: the page splits its tile request so it never exceeds the engine's 32,767 px limit -- DONE, no link was needed
items.note: SUPERSEDES the version of this item written on 2026-08-19 before the layer was corrected; that one asked which PAGE-SIDE step dropped the tile, and the premise was wrong -- no page-side step drops it, the engine returns an unpainted buffer above 32,767 px (see queue-long-document-renders-blank-in-silence and finding 062). What is owed is on the page after all, but it is not a bug hunt: layoutCanvas() sizes ONE canvas to the whole document and renderDocument() asks for ONE tile that size, so any document past about 33 pages at devicePixelRatio 1 -- or 17 at 2 -- requests something the engine will not paint. The fix is to stop doing that: render in strips no taller than 32,767, or use the TileScheduler that editor-session.js already imports. No link is needed. AND, separately, the product must not paint a tile it cannot verify: the engine reports success for an unpainted buffer, so a page that trusts the return value has no way to tell. Whatever the fix, it owes the user an error rather than a blank page -- that half is what makes a-long-document-is-drawn-or-the-product-says-it-is-not KNOWN_RED today. DONE 2026-08-19, shell v18. renderDocument() now issues one request per strip, none taller than MAX_TILE_HEIGHT = 32767, and composes them at their own y. A document short enough to fit takes exactly one strip covering the whole canvas, so nothing changes for the common case. Measured: 35 pages at dpr 1 (canvas 34,847) and the same 20-page document at dpr 2 (39,839) both draw, where both were blank; and there is no seam -- bands sampled at 32,300 / 32,600 / 32,900 and at the bottom are all fully opaque and all carry ink. Guarded by the `one-tile-for-the-whole-document` mutation, which puts the limit back to a million and turns the check red. ALSO ADDED: renderDocument() refuses a tile the engine did not paint (`TILE_NOT_PAINTED`), by sampling ALPHA at 512 points -- an unpainted buffer is all zeros including alpha, while a genuinely blank page is opaque white, so the two are told apart in a bounded number of reads on a buffer that can be a hundred megabytes. That is the half that makes the failure loud if the limit is ever hit again.

items.title: the engine returns an unpainted buffer above 32,767 px and reports success -- the product routes around it, the defect is still there
items.note: Measured at two widths whose buffers differ by a factor of two -- 45 MB paints at height 32,767 and 45 MB is blank at 32,768 -- so it is the height, not the memory, and 32,767 = 2^15-1. The buffer comes back exactly width x height x 4 bytes, ImageData builds from it, and render() does not throw: the engine says it succeeded. The product no longer hits this (it splits its request into strips) and refuses an unpainted tile if it ever does, so nothing is blocked -- but a client that asks for one still gets a silent lie, and a workaround in one caller is not a fix. WHERE in the engine is not established: that a 2^15 boundary is a signed 16-bit quantity is an inference from the number and no source at that point has been read. Worth an upstream look before it is called ours. ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-21, and the inference this item forbade asserting was WRONG. It is NOT a signed 16-bit quantity and NOT an overflow: it is Cairo's explicit image-surface size check, MAX_IMAGE_SIZE 32767 in workdir/UnpackedTarball/cairo/src/cairo-image-surface.c:59, whose own comment says the reason is that pixman coordinates are 16.16 fixed point (pixman_fixed_t is int32_t, not int16_t). It applies to WIDTH equally -- our widths were simply always under it. Chain, each hop read: Cairo returns a nil/error surface (CAIRO_STATUS_INVALID_SIZE); SvpSalVirtualDevice::CreateSurface (vcl/headless/svpvd.cxx:107-111) converts that to false and SAL_WARN_IFs; VirtualDevice returns it (vcl/source/gdi/virdev.cxx:384); and desktop/source/lib/init.cxx:4288 DISCARDS the bool and paints on the error surface at :4292. The LOK ABI's paintTile is void, and doc_paintTile clears the last-error string on entry and never sets it again. Drawing on a Cairo error context is a documented no-op, so the buffer comes back exactly width*height*4 bytes and untouched -- the zeros are our own malloc. No clamp: 32768 is refused, not reduced. Our build reaches this path (config_vclplug.h ENABLE_HEADLESS 1 / USE_HEADLESS_CODE 1; LOK forces SAL_USE_VCLPLUGIN=svp at init.cxx:8273). UPSTREAM: the dimension limit is a real constraint a caller must respect (our product already splits into strips); the SILENT completion is an upstream error-propagation defect, and LibreOfficeKit.hxx:136-142 documents no limit. A minimal upstream statement is drafted in findings/evidence/062/layer/ATTRIBUTION.md; submission stays on hold. Method: delegated to codex, then the crux was re-read directly before being accepted. CLOSED 2026-08-22 in the v4 link work. `handlePaintTile` refuses before allocating when either dimension exceeds 32767, with `TILE_EXCEEDS_ENGINE_LIMIT` and a message naming the requested size. The limit is ATTRIBUTED, not inferred from the number: Cairo's `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` at cairo-image-surface.c:59, whose own comment gives the reason (pixman coordinates are 16.16 fixed-point). It is not a signed 16-bit height and not an overflow, and it applies to WIDTH equally -- so both are checked. The engine has to refuse rather than forward a failure because LOK's paintTile returns void: SVP computes a correct boolean and doc_paintTile (init.cxx:4288) discards it. That upstream defect still stands; this makes our layer stop reporting success over it.
items.checkNote: Watching for the engine learning to refuse, or to paint, above the limit -- under a name that does not exist today.

items.title: cut removes text -- CLOSED 2026-08-22 on the linked v4 artifact, by a manifest widening with a four-shape characterisation behind it. No relink.
items.source: finding 063; measured 2026-08-19 once the harness had a clipboard
items.note: The product's cut is copy-then-delete in that order, deliberately. The copy works. The delete is refused every time, because the ten v1 actions are declared caret-only in the manifest (tools/build_e2_b_profile.py:86 -- 'range dispatch was characterised for the paragraph actions, not for delete or insert') and a cut runs on a range by definition. So cut is effectively copy. The disposition half of this was finding 063 and is fixed; this item is the CAPABILITY half. The fix is not simply to widen the manifest: what the declaration is missing is the measurement behind it. Either characterise range delete for the v1 actions and then declare it, or add an action that deletes a selection. NOT a link either way -- gestures are a manifest choice (probe_engine.cpp says so where the mask is defined). MEASURED 2026-08-21 and the remedy NARROWS: widening the manifest is not enough, and the run says so. With BOTH range bits granted to delete-backward in a MIRRORED manifest (dist/ untouched, probe.wasm byte-identical to 29ec627b), the EDITOR_FORMAT_GESTURE_UNSUPPORTED refusal disappears -- confirming the caret-only declaration was what produced it -- and the SELECTION BARRIER refuses instead: EDITOR_STATE_UNAVAILABLE, 'selection barrier requires a callback-confirmed collapsed caret'. The session goes to recoverable-error and the save that would have answered 'was the text removed' is refused with EDITOR_NOT_READY, so whether the engine CAN remove a range is still NOT established. Two runs, identical. Evidence and the pre-written prediction: findings/evidence/queue-cut-cannot-remove-text/. Consequence: the remedy is engine-side either way -- a barrier that can confirm a RANGE, or a distinct delete-selection action -- so this item moves next to redo/move-by-line/select-all in the ABI proposal and is NO LONGER no-link work. The old note's 'NOT a link either way' is superseded by this measurement. Re-ask with `run_e2_c_product_path.py --range-delete-diagnostic` after any engine change. SECOND ARM 2026-08-21 (fable proposed cut might need no engine work at all, because the empty-text refusal looked JS-only): MEASURED, and the route is CLOSED IN COMPILED CODE. Four layers, each removed in a mirror until the next appeared: document-sdk.js:468 (JS guard); sdk-worker.js:352 withWasmBytes throwing on a zero-length allocation (JS, and incidental -- a generic allocation-failure check, not a policy about empty text); and then src/sdk_api.cpp:172-174, which returns OXSDK_STATUS_INVALID_ARGUMENT when utf8Length == 0. That is the engine's own ABI boundary. handleReplaceSelection (probe_engine.cpp:3199-3216) really does have no empty-text gate, and is unreachable -- reading the handler without its export wrapper is what made the route look open. Session survived, document unchanged, neighbours intact. CONSEQUENCE: cut STAYS in the link payload as a DISTINCT delete-selection action, id 20, gestures range-single + range-cross only, so delete-backward's measured caret-only characterisation is untouched. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: whether LOK's paste with zero-length text deletes a selection -- no arm has reached it, and it is worth one probe inside the link work, because if it does then delete-selection can relax sdk_api.cpp's length check and reuse handleReplaceSelection instead of writing a new barrier entry. The fallback is the barrier-entry route: startSelectionBarrierDelete (:3143-3151) refuses a pre-existing selection BY DESIGN, then posts shift+Left/Right to manufacture its own unit, and verified-selection-delete already has the capture/dispatch/verify stages. Evidence: findings/evidence/queue-cut-cannot-remove-text/PREDICTION-replace-selection.md + RESULT-replace-selection.md. 2026-08-22, v4 link work: the ENGINE HALF has shipped and the ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS REPLACED, but the item stays ABSENT because nothing has been measured yet. delete-selection is wire id 20 in the v4 contract, granted `range-single` ONLY: `collapsed` is withheld because a delete-selection with no selection would duplicate delete-backward and quietly widen the one action here that has a characterisation behind it, and `range-cross` is withheld because nobody has measured a cross-paragraph delete. That narrows the note above, which said range-single + range-cross -- it said so before the measurement existed, and the rule is the other one. Granting range-cross later costs a measurement, not a relink. The old check wanted RANGE_DELETE_CHARACTERISED in tools/build_e2_b_profile.py, which is the OTHER remedy -- widening the v1 actions' own gestures -- and this design rejected it precisely so delete-backward's caret-only characterisation stays untouched. That file is not edited by this link at all, so the check could never have gone green. It is replaced by one that goes green when the thing this item is actually about is measured: a product-path check that cut REMOVES the text. CLOSED 2026-08-22, AND THE CLOSING MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THE SHIPPED DECLARATION RATHER THAN JUST CONFIRMING IT. `range-single` alone is not a narrower grant, it is an OFF SWITCH: probe_engine.cpp gates an unclassified selection on `range_single AND range_cross`, so from the link until today the engine refused EVERY cut with "this action is not offered for this kind of selection in this profile" -- a sentence true of no selection at all. A manifest that declares a gesture the binary will never honour is the "describes but does not constrain" defect pointing the other way, and it is worse than either extreme because it reads as a deliberate narrowing. Pre-registered predictions all held (PREDICTION.md): the refusal disappears; a within-paragraph range is removed with both neighbours verbatim and the document still parsing; the session stays ready and can still save. P-CUT-4 carried no prediction by design and was MEASURED ON FOUR SHAPES -- two paragraphs, three paragraphs into a bullet list, a bullet list through a plain paragraph into a numbered list, and within one list. Every arm merged the way a word processor does: head of the first paragraph plus tail of the last, line count down by exactly the number of boundaries crossed, every untouched paragraph verbatim, session `ready`, document readable. Across three runs the shipped 34 checks moved in exactly one place, and that place was this check's own obsolete oracle. The 2026-08-21 arm that ended in recoverable-error was `delete-backward` through the selection barrier; delete-selection dispatches .uno:Delete plainly and deliberately, which is why the ABI 4 design was a distinct action rather than a widening -- that decision is now measured, not argued. Repackage only: wasm f923cfa5, loader c382b834 and worker e6ee92ca all byte-identical; manifest f88c6289 -> cbf93923. Evidence: findings/evidence/queue-cut-cannot-remove-text/RESULT-range-cross.md.

items.title: there is no select-all action, so Ctrl+A is not bound
items.source: measured 2026-08-19 while wiring the keyboard row
items.note: The contract has fifteen actions and none of them selects everything. Expressing it geometrically was tried and MEASURED: selectRange from (0,0) to the document's width and height reports success in about half a second, the engine still reports the selection collapsed, and the canvas shows no selection wash. Present-with-no-gestures, NOT omitted: the engine initialises every entry to all-permitted on the first mask call, so an omitted action would ship wide open while the manifest looked silent about it. Item stays ABSENT and the check is unchanged, which is the honest state: the client must not bind Ctrl+A to something the engine refuses every time, and this item is about the SHORTCUT, not about the id. items.title: the page reads the caret before the cursor callback lands and nothing asks again -- a product-path race, not an engine defect
items.note: MEASURED, seven runs, 2 PASS / 7. `gEditorState.caret` is written ONLY when LOK_CALLBACK_INVALIDATE_VISIBLE_CURSOR arrives (probe_engine.cpp:2226), and handleInsertText replies immediately after paste() (:2809) without waiting for any callback. The control is in the same file: the key-movement path sets gEditorPending.requiredCallback and completes ON the callback, which is why a move always produces a fresh caret and a commit does not. The counter names the missing one: `sourceSequence` advances by TWO across a commit whose caret stays put and by THREE across one whose caret follows, so the third callback is the cursor one and it is absent 5/7. paint() reported drew-caret in all seven runs -- the page is not declining to draw, it is drawing the rectangle it was given. NOT ESTABLISHED and it gates the remedy: whether LOK's paste emits that callback unreliably, or emits it with a payload that fails to parse. The engine already tells those apart -- a cursor-range callback that does not parse emits `editor-callback-parse-error` (:2316) -- and nobody has looked for that event during a commit. THAT MEASUREMENT NEEDS NO LINK; do it first. Two remedy candidates, both engine and both blocked on it: (a) make handleInsertText wait for the cursor callback, which hangs if the callback never comes; (b) commit via postKeyEvent instead of paste -- that path already exists as paste's fallback and key events do move the cursor -- which needs the cost to IME and long strings measured, and needs to know why paste was chosen. DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE v4 PAYLOAD: that payload is gated and green, and an unverified engine change whose mechanism is still one measurement short is exactly what 'accumulate the payload and ship once' exists to keep out. SUPERSEDED THE SAME DAY BY A DEEPER MEASUREMENT, and the attribution above is WRONG: the engine is fine. Four more runs with the worker's `editor-state` and `editor-callback-parse-error` forwards ungated in a mirror show the engine emitting `visible-cursor` with the CORRECT rectangle (caretX 3131) at sourceSequence 6, promptly, in every run, with zero parse errors. What is stale is the PAGE's snapshot: the drain does `result?.state || await getState()` once per queued operation and insert replies immediately after paste(), so the page's last getState is answered at sourceSequence 5 -- one before the cursor callback. Nothing asks again, because the engine's own editor-state announcement is DROPPED BY THE WORKER on a product profile (`editorDiscoveryEnabled()` is false; the builder pops `diagnostic` from the manifest). That accounts for all eleven runs: the two that passed had their last getState answered at sequence 6. CONSEQUENCE: not an engine change and NOT A LINK. The remedy is in the worker plus the session. But sdk-worker.js IS one of the five identities a profile binds, so a worker fix landed BEFORE the ABI 4 link ships inside that profile at no extra cost -- and unlike an engine change it can be verified in a mirror first, which is the condition for putting anything into a gated payload. Evidence: findings/evidence/068/caret-after-commit/ (README second half). FIXED IN SOURCE AND VERIFIED 2026-08-22, still ABSENT here because the fix has not SHIPPED: half of it is in sdk-worker.js, and the v3 profile's copy of that file is frozen. The remedy is two changes, both outside the engine: the worker forwards `editor-state` on every profile rather than only a discovery one (exposing nothing new -- every field is already in the product's own editorGetStateV2 reply), and editor-shell-v2/narrow-editor-v2-session.js overrides _handleEngineEvent to adopt it, guarded on sourceSequence advancing and on the session being ready or busy. The override is deliberate: the natural home was EditorSession._handleEngineEvent and check_e1_c_bundle_intact.py refused it, because that file is bound to E1-C's verdict (shell bundle 187706b2...). Measured, same arm throughout: 2/7 with neither change, 0/4 with the worker half alone (nothing was listening), 5/5 with both, 4/4 again after the fix moved to the subclass. Shell bundle v30. The worker half ships with the ABI 4 link at no extra cost, because that builder hashes whichever worker is in the tree. CLOSED 2026-08-22 ON THE LINKED ARTIFACT. The worker half shipped with the ABI 4 profile (e2-editor-v4, worker e6ee92ca) and the product path now carries `caret-follows-the-text-you-type`: PASS 3/3, with the control holding (the sink tracks the caret at all: 132 -> 506 between a click near the line start and one past its end). Read from `#sink`'s offset, which finding 069 pinned to the caret, so the caret's position is now a DOM observable; the stated limit is that this is the position the page draws FROM, not the pixels it drew -- `the-caret-is-drawn-where-it-was-placed` is the other half. THREE ROUNDS because the defect was intermittent at 2/7 and a single round would report green about a fifth of the time. Two things the first runs of this check corrected, both in the check and not in the product: its oracle asked for a larger `left` and round 1 failed at 617 -> 296 because the typing WRAPPED (a wrapped caret is ahead of where it was, so the oracle is now forward-in-reading-order); and it sat among checks that aim by BAND INDEX while typing 36 characters into the fixture, which made `ctrl-x` see 9 bands one round and 8 the next -- moved to a point where nothing downstream aims by band.

items.title: finding 063's refusal path is no longer reachable through the product now that the gesture is granted -- the coverage moved into a mutation and that is weaker
items.source: 2026-08-22, recorded on the day the widening removed it; same shape as queue-recovery-path-lost-its-inducer
items.note: Finding 063 is that a REFUSED cut used to send the session into recoverable-error and tell the user to discard unsaved work, over an action that declared it had dispatched nothing. The disposition was fixed and `ctrl-x-is-handled-by-the-product` verified it on every run: the refusal is reported with its reason, the document is untouched, the session stays `ready`. Widening delete-selection to both range bits removes the refusal from the product's own path, so that check could no longer be about it and was replaced by `cut-removes-the-selected-text`. THE COVERAGE IS NOT GONE BUT IT IS WEAKER: the refusal path is now driven only by the `cut-falls-back-to-the-caret-only-delete` mutation, which runs when somebody names it rather than on every run, and a mutation asserts that a check goes RED -- it does not assert that the refusal was reported, the document untouched and the session alive. This is the third instance of the same structure in this tree (finding 046's disposition softening, finding 038's inducer, now this), and the rule it keeps teaching is that a fix removes the state its own regression check needed. Two candidates for a route that does not depend on breaking the product: drive an action the manifest withholds deliberately -- `select-all` ships with `gestures: []` and would be refused by the engine with the same code -- but the product does not offer it, so reaching it needs a page that dispatches an action `offers()` says no to, which is test-only behaviour in the product; or add a diagnostic-flag arm that narrows one action in a MIRROR the way --range-delete-diagnostic widens one, and assert finding 063's three properties there. The second costs no product change and reuses machinery that already exists. ROUTE BUILT 2026-08-22, NOT YET MEASURED -- and the item stays open for exactly that reason. The second candidate is in: `--refusal-diagnostic` narrows one action to `gestures: []` in a symlink mirror (present and empty, never removed -- deleting it would ship it wide open), and the check `a-refused-action-is-reported-and-changes-nothing` asserts all four of 063's properties: the refusal is reported with its reason, the saved document is unchanged, the session stays `ready`, and saving still works. The fourth is not decoration -- 063's harm was a notice telling the user to discard unsaved work, so a session that reports `ready` and cannot save has failed 063 while passing a state check. The narrowing reproduces the ORIGINAL path rather than an approximation: `offers()` reads an empty gesture list as withheld, so the page falls back to `delete-backward` exactly as it did on v3. The first candidate stays rejected, and a third was found and rejected BY READING: a cut on a collapsed caret would dispatch against a caret-only gesture set with no mirror at all, but `clipboard-adapter.js:69` throws CLIPBOARD_EMPTY_SELECTION before the delete is reached, and that ordering is deliberate. Mutation `cut-swallows-the-refusal` puts 063's discard back inside the operation where `run()` cannot see it; it carries `requiresFlag` and tests/test_product_path_mutations.py enforces that the flag exists, because run without it the mutation changes no observable and would report 'the product survived it' -- which is what a DEAD mutation reports. WHY STILL ABSENT: none of it has been run. Coverage that has never executed is not coverage, which is the finding this queue item's own neighbour (`cut-swallows-its-failure`) was written about. Criteria are fixed in findings/evidence/queue-cut-refusal-lost-its-inducer/PREDICTION.md, written before the run; the run waits for the a11y gate 0 core build to stop holding twelve cores, because this net has timing-sensitive terms. MEASURED 2026-08-26 AND CLOSED, both ways, on the shipped e2-editor-v8, chrome. REFUSAL ARM: all four of finding 063's properties held on one run -- the toast named EDITOR_FORMAT_GESTURE_UNSUPPORTED, the saved document was unchanged, the session stayed `ready`, and the save after the refusal produced a readable ODT. The run as a whole was 38 PASS / 2 NOT_ESTABLISHED, ok true, and the second abstention is `cut-removes-the-selected-text` -- correct and predicted, since this arm withholds the delete. MUTATION ARM: `cut-swallows-the-refusal` turned the check RED on the term it moves (`refusalReported: false`) while the other three stayed true, and the product SAID IT HAD CUT (`已剪下 …`) over an action that removed nothing -- finding 063's user-facing shape, on demand. `the mutation was detected by the check that owns it`, ok true. Evidence: findings/evidence/queue-cut-refusal-lost-its-inducer/RESULT.md plus both reports and step traces. The prediction was written 2026-08-22 and is unedited below its status line.

items.title: the product-path coverage audit cannot see a second listener for an event name it already knows -- measured 2026-08-22 when one arrived
items.source: finding 073; noticed while registering the composition listeners the audit DID catch
items.note: `tools/audit_product_path_coverage.py` enforces page minus driven minus waived is empty, and it did its job on 2026-08-22: three new composition listeners failed the build until they were registered. But it keys on the EVENT NAME. Finding 073 added a fourth listener in the same edit -- `blur` on #sink, to hide an abandoned IME composition -- and `listener:blur` was already registered (for the global `endDrag(null)` handler), so it arrived silently and appears in the report as covered by an entry about a different handler on a different element. Nothing was wrong with either entry; the GRANULARITY is the hole. Any listener whose event name is already in the registry can be added without the audit noticing, and this tree has three findings (049, 050, the unbound Ctrl+C) that were exactly 'a handler nobody had exercised'. The remedy is to key on target+event rather than event -- the parser already sees `el.sink.addEventListener("blur"` and `globalThis.addEventListener("blur"` as distinct text, so the datum exists and is being discarded. Cost: every existing registry entry needs its target written in, which is why this is recorded rather than done in the same commit as the finding it came out of. DONE 2026-08-22. The hand-kept NAMED_ELEMENTS table is gone rather than extended: `listener_target()` derives the name from the receiver (`el.noticeAction` -> `notice-action`, `globalThis` -> `global`), which reproduces every name that table gave, so this is a rename for thirteen paths and a SPLIT for one -- `listener:blur` became `listener:blur#global` (endDrag, uncovered as before) and `listener:blur#sink` (073's hideComposition, uncovered with its own risk and the route to driving it named). A table cannot be forgotten for the sixth element if there is no table. Two mutations prove the granularity can fail -- deleting either blur listener now reddens the audit, and under the old keying BOTH would have stayed green because a `listener:blur` remained either way. One hole found while in here and closed in the same edit: the parser only sees `el.<name>` and `globalThis`, so a listener on `document` or a local variable was not narrowed but INVISIBLE, and invisible reads as full coverage; the audit now counts what it cannot attribute and refuses. The self-test also counts its own checks instead of carrying a hand-written total, which was already one short of the lines it printed.

items.title: a paragraph whose listPrefixLength equals its contentLength fingerprints as the EMPTY STRING, so two of them are indistinguishable -- measured on the heading, 2026-08-22
items.source: a11y gate 0's own run, three times identically (findings/evidence/a11y-gate-0/RESULT.md)
items.note: The engine fingerprints a focused paragraph as FNV-1a 64 over the body AFTER stripping listPrefixLength characters (probe_engine.cpp:1614-1667). On `E1-LC-HEADING` LOK reported listPrefixLength 13 against contentLength 13 -- the whole paragraph as prefix -- so the hashed body was empty and the fingerprint came back cbf29ce484222325, the FNV-1a offset basis. That constant already has a meaning in this tree: it is what EVERY paragraph reported when the basis was mistyped on 2026-08-17, i.e. it is the value that means UNFED. So the failure mode is not a wrong answer, it is an answer that cannot be told apart from a broken one, and any two such paragraphs share it. It did NOT move the gate verdict: the criterion asks for >= 2 distinct identities matching their targets and placements 1 and 2 supply that, matching both hash and length against the fixture's own XML. TWO HYPOTHESES, NEITHER MEASURED, AND NO LAYER IS NAMED (040, 048, 062): LOK reports the prefix that way for an outline-numbered heading, or our parse of the focused-paragraph JSON mis-assigns the field. The cheap discriminator is the NATIVE build -- build-native-26-8 has the same LOK, provides accessibility already, and needs no rebuild; tools/queue_native_a11y_attach_timing.cpp is the existing place to ask it from. This matters most to roadmap 3.4 and to block identity, both of which would read the fingerprint as an identity. ONE HYPOTHESIS ELIMINATED 2026-08-23, for free, by opening the text (roadmap 3.4 route B): the same heading now reports `paragraphText: "E1-LC-HEADING"` alongside `contentLength: 13` and `listPrefixLength: 13`. The text LOK carried IS the heading's own text, and the parse reads `listPrefixLength` straight out of the payload by name -- so 'our parse mis-assigns the field' is out. What remains is on LOK's side and is still two things, which is why this stays open: either LOK genuinely reports the whole heading as list prefix, or the field means something other than what this engine assumes it means. The native build is still the discriminator. SEPARATELY, the CONSEQUENCE is now smaller for 3.4 specifically: a projection that has the text does not need the fingerprint to READ a paragraph, only to compare one -- so the collapse costs identity, not readability. ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-23 BY READING THE CORE SOURCE, and it is upstream: finding 074. `sfx2/source/view/viewsh.cxx:554-588` `getListPrefixSize()` returns `aTextSegment.SegmentEnd` for the ATTRIBUTE_RUN at index 0 -- the end of the FIRST ATTRIBUTE RUN, not the length of the numbering prefix. The two coincide only when the prefix is its own run, which is why bullet lists usually look fine (`"\u2022 "` has different character attributes). A numbered paragraph with uniform character formatting is ONE run, so SegmentEnd is the whole paragraph length -- and a heading is the common case, because it carries an outline number (so nLevel >= 0 and bIsCounted pass the guard at :579) and is usually formatted uniformly. So neither hypothesis needed the native build in the end: it is LOK, and it is one line. The native comparison is no longer the discriminator and this item does not need it. WHAT STAYS OPEN: our side still has to decide what to do about it, and that is not the same question -- the fingerprint is unusable as an identity for a SECOND, independent reason (paragraphs with identical text share one, measured: 22% of paragraphs in the r7-compat corpus sit in a collision), so fixing 074 upstream would not make a fingerprint join workable. DECIDED AND DONE 2026-08-26, and the decision was forced rather than chosen: the collapsed fingerprint reached the format barrier's identity gate and refused a CORRECT `set-paragraph-body` on that very heading -- `MUTATION_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` with a rollback disposition, on a session with no checkpoint, four runs out of four on `e2-editor-v9`. That is FINDING 082, and it is what this item's 'our side still has to decide what to do about it' turned into. WHAT WAS DECIDED: a degenerate fingerprint is not a reading, so no consumer in this engine may treat it as an identity. `src/a11y_paragraph_identity.hpp` holds the rule beside the hash; `paragraphFingerprintIsUsable(listPrefixLength, contentLength)` is false when a NON-EMPTY paragraph reports its whole length as prefix, and the barrier's gate DECLINES the comparison rather than failing it -- the same fail-open the surrounding comment already argued for, extended from 'the value is absent' to 'the value is present and meaningless'. A genuinely empty paragraph keeps its fingerprint, because the empty hash is the correct reading of an empty paragraph and the barrier already declares two of them indistinguishable. The editor state now carries `a11y.fingerprintUsable` and the barrier payload carries `dispatchUsable`/`readbackUsable`/`declined`, so a host outside the engine can tell the two apart too -- which is what this item was really about. AUDITED: the identity gate is the only place in probe_engine.cpp that COMPARES two fingerprints; every other site reports or clears the value. MEASURED: `tests/a11y_paragraph_identity_test.cpp` runs on the host and reproduces six fingerprints the accessibility engine really reported, including the collision (`E1-LC-HEADING` 13/13 and `• ` 2/2 both `cbf29ce484222325`) and the case that had to survive (a paragraph and the same paragraph with a bullet share `76f09d751bb341f7`); four mutations of the rule are each detected. Linked as `e2-editor-v10`, one variable against v9, and the product path there runs all 40 checks with the paragraph-format arm PASSING six of six. WHAT STAYS OPEN AND IS NOT THIS ITEM: finding 074 upstream is untouched -- the number is still wrong and every other consumer of `listPrefixLength` is still exposed -- and the fingerprint is still unusable as an identity for the second, independent reason this item already records (22% of the r7-compat corpus collides on text alone).
items.checkNote: Five, and the middle two are the load-bearing ones: the rule can exist, be tested, and be wired to nothing -- which is exactly what a plausible tidy-up would leave behind. One pins the gate's own extra condition, the other pins the point where the flag is computed from the two counts. The last two pin the host test into the tree AND into the target that runs it, because a test nobody runs is the same silence as no test. Deliberately NOT pinned: anything about finding 074, which is upstream and not ours to flip.

items.title: paragraphFresh reports true on a core with accessibility compiled out -- the same capability-failure-as-data defect one level below the one that was just fixed
items.source: found 2026-08-22 by running the PRODUCT-profile control that the a11y gate needed; findings/evidence/a11y-gate-0/RESULT.md
items.note: MEASURED, not read: on `e2-editor-v4` all three caret placements came back `enabled: false`, `unavailable: "core-built-without-accessibility"` -- which is `queue-engine-must-report-core-lacks-accessibility` working -- AND `paragraphFresh: true`, contentLength 0, fingerprint cbf29ce484222325 (the FNV-1a offset basis). The mechanism: on a stripped core every LOK entry point still EXISTS, getA11yFocusedParagraph() returns a well-formed empty answer (`content: ""`, `position: 0`), and `parseEditorSemanticJson` returns true because its postcondition is `position >= 0 && contentLength >= 0`. So the engine recorded a successful reading of nothing. `fresh` is THE bit that says 'the last read succeeded, so the fingerprint describes where the caret is NOW' -- a host that gates on it, which is what the field is for, takes the empty-string fingerprint for a live identity. That is the same shape as the `enabled: true` defect, one level down, and it matters directly to roadmap 3.4: an ARIA projection decides whether to trust the fingerprint by reading exactly this bit. FIXED IN SOURCE: `refreshCaretParagraph()` now returns early with the fields cleared unless `gEditorAccessibilityEnabled`. Gated on the flag rather than a second `#if` so it also covers the runtime cases (no document, LOK missing an entry point) where the answer is equally not a reading. Syntax-checked against BOTH core configs. IT DOES NOT REACH THE PRODUCT UNTIL A LINK -- dist/ still carries the old behaviour, and that is the honest state; ride along with the next link, exactly as its predecessor did. LINK PREPARED 2026-08-24 as `e2-editor-v8` -- Makefile targets, archive of the shipped v7, pre-link gates all green, runbook at handoff/RUNBOOK-relink-v8.md. The link command itself is the user's. What that link ships was MEASURED rather than read (tools/what_the_link_ships.py --since eab775c, evidence at findings/evidence/f076-what-the-link-ships/): three things, not one -- this fix, the other of these two items, and 21 code lines of additive a11y forwarding in sdk-worker.js that the builder hashes because it is in the tree. Reading the #ifdefs would have found only the first. THIS ITEM STAYS OPEN UNTIL A RUN: the source check passes today, and what it asserts is that the source carries the fix, not that the product behaves.
items.checkNote: Two checks because either alone is weak: the guard could be typed without clearing the fields, and the clearing already existed on the failed-read path. `atLeast: 2` is what says there are now two paths that clear rather than one.

items.title: the product page's editorState is the RAW engine state -- a11y counters and schedulerProbe included -- which is what E1-B bans, and productEditorState never reaches it
items.note: MEASURED, not read: across three caret placements the page's `snapshot.editorState` carried `a11y` and `schedulerProbe` every time and `caretParagraph` none of the times. Two writers disagree about the shape. `productEditorState` is applied to the v2 ACTIONS' replies and to `editorGetStateV1`; the product's own `editorGetStateV2` falls through to the raw branch, and the `editor-state` ANNOUNCEMENT -- which fires on every engine state change and is gated only on a rising sourceSequence -- is the writer that wins in practice. So the same datum reaches the page under two names depending on which reply landed last, and a consumer cannot know which one it holds. E1-B section: '不把a11y diagnostic counters、scheduler probe或raw callback payload升格為產品state' -- on today's page they are promoted. PARTIALLY MITIGATED 2026-08-23, additively: the announcement now also carries `caretParagraph`, derived from the same `productEditorState` the actions use rather than from a second copy of the rule, and the v2 session override copies it through. That gives 3.4's projection one name that is always present. IT DOES NOT CLOSE THIS: the raw fields are still on the page, the two operations still answer in two shapes, and `editorGetStateV2` still bypasses the projection. Removing them is the right end state and a wider change -- `web/e2-c-d2-app.js` issues editorGetStateV2 directly, and the diagnostic harnesses read raw fields -- so it wants a round that can measure what it breaks rather than a late-night edit beside a feature.
items.checkNote: Absent until editorGetStateV2 is routed through the product projection like the actions and editorGetStateV1 are. That string appearing is the smallest honest signal that the asymmetry was addressed rather than described.

items.title: a projected list item carries its own bullet in the text, so a screen reader announces it twice -- and the obvious fix builds on the field finding 074 is about
items.note: The structure projection gives list paragraphs `role="listitem"` and the text the tree reports, which INCLUDES the prefix: `• E1-LC-BULLET-ONE`, `1. E1-LC-NUMBER-ONE`. An AT announces the bullet from the role, so the marker is read twice. The obvious remedy is to strip `listPrefixLength` characters, and it is deliberately NOT done: that field is exactly what finding 074 describes -- it returns the end of the first ATTRIBUTE RUN, not the prefix length. Measured 2026-08-23 it is correct for the two list shapes in list-contexts (2 and 3) and returns 13 for a heading whose true prefix is 0. Two samples that happened to be right is not a licence to slice text on a field with a known upstream defect. Routes, none measured: strip only when `role == PARAGRAPH && isNumbered` (narrower, still trusts the field); ask for the numbering label separately; or wait for 074 upstream. Cosmetic on its face and it is not -- double announcement is one of the things that makes a screen reader unusable in practice, and it will be judged against the 68 檢測碼 rather than against taste.
items.checkNote: Absent until the page slices a prefix at all. When it does, the diff has to say which route was taken and why the 074 risk is acceptable there.

items.title: the tile pixel buffer is malloc'd, paintTile draws only the page, and putImageData blits the rest -- uninitialised heap, in colour, on a canvas the user can screenshot
items.source: finding 076, found 2026-08-23 while tracing finding 075's root cause; findings/evidence/f075-off-page-garbage/
items.note: MEASURED, not read. `putImageData` is replace semantics INCLUDING alpha, and `layoutCanvas()` scales the whole canvas without cropping, so whatever malloc returned outside the page is displayed. It has always happened and was invisible because a freshly grown WASM heap is zero: the project had already measured the shipped core's unpainted buffer at 88 non-zero of 2,105,340 sampled points (0.0042%) and 0% opaque, which is why the ink test never saw it. On the accessibility core the same off-page columns came back 290 opaque of 26,941 (1.08%) with 184 distinct alpha values against 33 -- 250x as much of the same thing, plausibly because +19.9 MB of code means this buffer lands on REUSED memory rather than a fresh page (that last part is inference, not measured). 31 of those pixels were dark enough to be ink and broke the band scan, which is finding 075 and the cheap half; the expensive half is that fragments of this process's heap were being rendered. FIXED IN SOURCE with `calloc` rather than a later memset, so there is no window and no second statement to forget. Syntax-checked with em++ under BOTH configurations (writer-only and a11y). IT DOES NOT REACH THE PRODUCT UNTIL A LINK -- dist/ still carries malloc. The harness-side page clip from finding 075 stays regardless: it guards the class of defect, not this one instance, and a purely engine-side fix would leave the instrument silently wrong on the next unexpected off-page rendering. LINK PREPARED 2026-08-24 as `e2-editor-v8` -- Makefile targets, archive of the shipped v7, pre-link gates all green, runbook at handoff/RUNBOOK-relink-v8.md. The link command itself is the user's. What that link ships was MEASURED rather than read (tools/what_the_link_ships.py --since eab775c, evidence at findings/evidence/f076-what-the-link-ships/): three things, not one -- this fix, the other of these two items, and 21 code lines of additive a11y forwarding in sdk-worker.js that the builder hashes because it is in the tree. Reading the #ifdefs would have found only the first. THIS ITEM STAYS OPEN UNTIL A RUN: the source check passes today, and what it asserts is that the source carries the fix, not that the product behaves. CLOSED 2026-08-24 ON THE CORE THAT SHOWED IT. Shipping in e2-editor-v8 proved less than it looked like: the PRODUCT core already read as transparent off-page under malloc, so a clean canvas there is `no regression`, not `cured`. So `a11y-calloc` was linked -- the v5 lineage with the one line changed, and single-variable by measurement rather than intent: loader, worker, soffice.data and its metadata all byte-identical to e2-editor-v5, manifests differing only in profile, sdkVersion and wasmSha256, and the wasm difference confirmed as one hunk by the preprocessor. Off-page pixels, 26,941 per shot: v5 goes 3 -> 290 -> 1,235 opaque across at-rest / after-caret / after-an-edit, with 853 of the last dark enough to be ink; a11y-calloc is 0 / 0 / 0. The post-fix rows equal the product core's own to the pixel, and the baseline reproduces 075's archived numbers on a different profile. Also learned: the defect was WORSE than 075 recorded, which measured only at-rest and after-caret -- nobody had driven an edit. Evidence: findings/evidence/f076-calloc-on-the-core-that-showed-it/.
items.checkNote: Both directions, because adding the calloc without removing the malloc is exactly the shape of a half-applied fix -- and the absent check is what makes a revert visible.

items.title: the four inline formats are offered for `collapsed` only, so selected text cannot be emboldened -- and the regression net is green because it asks the manifest what to test
items.source: finding 078, found 2026-08-23 by the operator pressing bold on a selection in the v5 preview and getting EDITOR_FORMAT_GESTURE_UNSUPPORTED
items.note: RESOLVED AND SHIPPED as e2-editor-v7 (2026-08-23, commit be8291a). The characterisation is done -- all four inline formats, both range shapes, formatted text equal to selected text, on the minted identity itself, with a native-LibreOffice comparison showing the paragraph-level shape on a fully selected paragraph is what native writes too. BOTH range bits are granted because the engine requires both for an unclassified range; granting one alone admits nothing, measured three ways (single-only refused, cross-only refused, both accepted). That AND-semantics limit is recorded in e2/expected-gesture-offers.json. The regression net now has `an-inline-format-reaches-a-selection` with a mutation that turns it red. The operator's real-mouse pass on all four buttons passed, which is what this project treats as closure, and the product page was pointed at v7 the same day.
items.checkNote: RE-PINNED 2026-08-24, and the reason is worth more than the fix. The first check pinned `"profile": "e2-editor-v7"` in the expectation file -- the profile NAME, which is exactly the field a cutover moves. Finding 076's link moved it to v8 and this item went DRIFTED while nothing about finding 078 had changed at all: the pin was on the paperwork rather than on the property. It is now on the property -- `set-bold` present in the expectation with `range-cross` among the gestures -- so a narrowing fails here and a rename does not. A pin that goes red at every routine link is a pin people learn to clear without reading.

items.title: the toolbar computes button availability from `lastSelectionShape`, which reads `collapsed` after EVERY drag because it is computed from two fields the v2 client's result does not carry
items.source: finding 079, found 2026-08-23 by a mutation that never fired
items.note: FIXED 2026-08-23 AND THE DIAGNOSIS CHANGED. It was recorded as a STALE value; it is not stale, there was never a value. `pumpDrag` read `result.collapsed` and `result.rectangles`, which is the shape `editor-shell/editor-client.js` builds on the V1 path. The v2 client returns the worker's envelope verbatim and the selection sits at `result.state.selection`, so both reads were `undefined`, `undefined === false` is false, `undefined?.length ?? 0` is 0, and the expression returned `collapsed` for every drag ever made. Measured on the shipped e2-editor-v7 with the engine's answer in the same arm (tools/probe_079_selection_shape.py): 12 code points selected inside one line and 34 across two while the page said `collapsed`, unchanged across an 8-second sampling window; after the fix, `range-single` and `range-cross`, both 52-55 ms after the pointer went down. A positive control that starts the variable at `range-single` proves the toolbar read can show a range at all. THE PREDICTED CONSEQUENCE WAS WRONG: `delete-selection` has no toolbar button and its only dispatch site asks the manifest, not the shape, so the cost lands on the six caret-only buttons instead, which stayed ENABLED while a range was selected. Shell-only; no link. The regression net gained `the-page-agrees-with-the-engine-about-the-selection` with the mutation `selection-shape-from-the-wrong-place`, which reintroduces the SILENT form. See also finding 080: this defect had been disarming `an-aborted-gesture-stops-selecting` since 2026-08-21. The derivation now lives in `selectionShapeOf` (editor-shell-v2/narrow-editor-v2-session.js) with unit tests whose fixtures are the RECORDED envelopes, one case of which is this finding: a v1-shaped object must come back unknown, never `collapsed`. Moved there on the external adjudicator's point that a DOM tripwire catches the next drift in one reader and does nothing about a second reader looking in a second wrong place.
items.checkNote: Three, and the first two are pinned as WHOLE lines so an `if (false && ...)` wrapped round either cannot satisfy a substring match -- this tree's own lesson. The accessor is pinned as well as the call site because the derivation was MOVED into editor-shell-v2 with its own tests, and pinning only the caller would let the read drift back to the wrong field one layer down. The third pins the defect's own expression as absent, so restoring it fails here even if the fixed lines are left beside it. The first version of these checks pinned a line that this same session then moved, and this check is what caught that -- which is the whole argument for pinning lines rather than trusting a note.

items.title: `an-aborted-gesture-stops-selecting` compared arms that had each aimed at a different line, so every margin it ever produced was noise
items.source: finding 080's re-aim, 2026-08-23; raised by the external adjudicator, not by the run
items.note: EXPLAINED AND FIXED 2026-08-23. Raised as three unexplained numbers -- a control whose reach moved 11 -> 6 between runs, a one-character margin where the coordinates predicted five, and a mutated arm that selected nothing rather than running to the end. ONE CAUSE: each arm called `stable_bands` for itself and took the first band wider than 40 px, and that scan is intermittent on this core (finding 075). The arms aimed at DIFFERENT LINES. Visible only once the selected TEXT was in the record beside the count: the control selected `1-LC-H` from band [83,182] while both abort arms selected `E1-LC-ISOL`. Different strings, no prefix relation possible, and the earlier run where this check PASSED passed by luck. FIXED in three steps, each of which the previous one made possible: (1) the aim is derived ONCE and shared by every arm, which is what makes them comparable at all; (2) with the comparison valid the weak strict-prefix predicate had no excuse, so a fourth REFERENCE arm now makes the same moves and stops where the others abort -- the expected answer is driven rather than predicted from pixels, which matters because the text is proportionally spaced; (3) the aim spans 90% of the widest band instead of half of the first band over 40 px, because the first run of the shared aim could not resolve (control selected `E1`, two characters, and the reference at half of that selected nothing) and abstained. MEASURED after all three, on the shipped page: control `E1-LC-ISOLATED 前後都不是清單`, reference `E1-LC-ISO`, and BOTH abort arms `E1-LC-ISO` -- byte-exact agreement with the reference, on a 14-vs-9 character margin. AND THE MUTATION IS NOW DETECTED FOR THE ORACLE'S OWN REASON, which it was not before: under `gesture-abort-not-wired` the control read `E1-LC-ISOLATED 前後都不是清單的`, the reference `E1-LC-ISOLAT`, the UNWIRED pointercancel arm the full `E1-LC-ISOLATED 前後都不是清單的` -- it followed the pointer to the end -- and the still-wired blur arm `E1-LC-ISOLAT`. One listener gone and one intact, differentiated inside a single run on a single line. Previously the detection came via an empty-string guard, which is a different property. BOTH DEBTS PAID 2026-08-26 -- read the paragraph below as the historical statement of what was owed, and then the settlement after it. WHAT WAS OWED: this is ONE run each way. An intermittent margin measured once gives a confident and wrong answer, and that is the whole history of this check. It wants N consecutive rounds before `the pointercancel and blur wiring is verified` is a sentence anyone may write. Also still unexamined: the reads are still synchronised on wall-clock sleeps rather than on the `revision` / `callbackSequence` fields the selectRange envelope already carries. SETTLED 2026-08-26, shipped e2-editor-v8, chrome, one machine, one sitting. EIGHT CONSECUTIVE PASS and THREE CONSECUTIVE DETECTIONS, and all eleven rounds aimed at the same line and selected the same strings -- control `E1-LC-ISOLATED 前後都不是清單的`, reference `E1-LC-ISOLAT`, both abort arms 12 code points on every green round. The three detections are the oracle's own reason each time: the arm whose pointercancel listener the mutation removes followed the pointer to the END (23 code points, byte-identical to the control) while the still-wired blur arm stopped at the reference's 12. So `the pointercancel and blur wiring is verified` is now a sentence somebody may write, and it rests on eleven rounds. THE SLEEPS ARE GONE, and the two fields this item named turned out not to be able to serve it -- MEASURED, not assumed: `revision` is the DOCUMENT's and a selection is not an edit, so it never advances on a selectRange; `callbackSequenceBefore/After` never leave the page's closure (`pumpDrag` publishes only `#toolbar[data-selection-shape]`, web/e2-editor-app.js:865), and publishing them is a product change and a shell generation for a field only a harness would read. What the page DOES publish is the answer, so both sleeps became polls on it and both waits are recorded per arm: the 0.8 s caret settle measures 0-1 ms and the 1.5 s copy wait measures 201-203 ms (200 ms poll granularity), so about 8.4 s per run was spent sleeping through an answer that had already arrived -- and a wait that starts taking seconds is now a measurement instead of a silence. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: anything about Firefox (every round is Chrome), and that the aim resolves on a document other than this fixture. Evidence: findings/evidence/queue-abort-margins-are-unexplained/RESULT-n-rounds.md plus the eleven per-round records beside it.
items.checkNote: Three. The first pins the queue id inside the check's own `doesNotEstablish` text, so a green that has quietly stopped declaring its limit fails here. The second pins the SHARED aim as a whole line -- re-deriving it per arm is the defect and it would come back as a plausible-looking tidy-up. The third pins the reference arm, without which the predicate silently weakens back to a strict prefix, which passed while the arms were reading different lines. A fourth, added 2026-08-26: it pins the COPY WAIT'S OWN MEASUREMENT into the arm's record. The poll that replaced `sleep(1.5)` is invisible from outside -- a tidy-up that put the sleep back would leave every string in this check identical and every round still green, and the only thing that would change is a number nobody was keeping. Now it is kept, and removing it fails here.

items.title: on the a11y core the product path keeps driving a session that is already in recoverable-error, so a run costs 20-50 minutes and produces no report at all
items.source: finding 081, measured 2026-08-24 by attaching to a live stalled run; fixed 2026-08-26
items.note: FIXED 2026-08-26, and the fix has a positive control that fakes nothing. THE STALL WAS NOT A HANG. Read off the stalled page over CDP on 2026-08-24: state=recoverable-error, checkpoint=none, latency='save failed', and PENDING=0 -- nothing was waiting on the engine. A save failed during `format-a-paragraph-changes-that-paragraph`, took the session into recoverable-error with no checkpoint, and every arm after it burned its own timeout against a session refusing everything with EDITOR_NOT_READY. That is the 20-50 minutes, and because the report was written only at the end the run yielded nothing at all. THE FIX IS THREE THINGS. (1) `Liveness`, a module-level guard: after every recorded check the page's state is read once, and `recoverable-error` or `restart-required` stops the run, names the check after which it noticed, lists in SOURCE ORDER the checks it never reached, and reports `ok: false` -- including under --mutate, where the mutation branch would otherwise conclude 'detected' from a run that stopped before the checks it was confounding. (2) The two arms that induce the dead state ON PURPOSE (finding 047's recipe and finding 038's endnote inducer) hold the guard off for exactly as long as they are inside themselves, and are READ ONCE MORE on the way out -- so an arm that fails to recover stops the run naming ITSELF rather than the innocent check that follows it. (3) `--out` is now written after every check with `complete: false`, so a run that is killed leaves a readable partial report instead of a zero-byte log. THE CONTROL, and it is the part that took the thinking: finding 081 does not reproduce on the shipped profile, so on every run this tree normally takes, a deleted guard and a working guard produce the same green report. `--liveness-control` stops the two inducing arms holding the guard off AND adds one probe inside each of them, at the point the arm has just wedged the engine and has not yet pressed the notice. The second half was found by running the first: a control built on the check boundaries alone went GREEN end to end, because both inducing arms recover before they record their check, so no boundary probe can ever meet the state they induce. The dead session the control then meets is REAL -- produced by the product's own buttons, read by the real guard, on the same page. Only the MOMENT is chosen. MEASURED 2026-08-26 on e2-editor-v8, chrome: guard armed, 37 PASS / 3 NOT_ESTABLISHED, `ok: true`, `liveness.probes: 39` -- which is 40 checks minus the 3 recorded inside the two held-off regions plus the 2 region-exit reads, so the guard is shown to have RUN and not merely to have not fired. tests/test_session_liveness.py drives the guard's four behaviours without a browser and is detected by six separate mutations of the guard. AND THEN IT FIRED ON ITS OWN, which is the measurement neither the control nor the unit test could be. Same day, `--profile e2-editor-v9`, no control flag, no mutation: the session died after `format-a-paragraph-changes-that-paragraph` -- the arm finding 081 named -- with state/pending/checkpoint/latency/toast IDENTICAL FIELD FOR FIELD to the CDP read taken off the live stalled run on 2026-08-24. `recorded: 17/40`, 23 arms not driven at a session refusing them, 322.3 s against the 20-50 minutes those stalls cost, and a readable report where there had been a zero-byte log. It also settled finding 081's open question: the first failure was `set-paragraph-body` returning `readback-is-a-different-paragraph` (probe_engine.cpp:4237, a branch gated on accessibility and therefore unreachable on the shipped core), and the save failure everyone could see was its consequence. FOUR RUNS, FOUR TIMES, IDENTICAL (three of them added afterwards with --barrier-details-diagnostic): every one dies after the same check with recorded 17/40, pending 0, checkpoint 無, and the same two arms -- set-paragraph-heading PASSES and set-paragraph-body fails with `readback-is-a-different-paragraph`. Filed as FINDING 082.
