items.title: `the-canvas-follows-a-document-that-grew` abstained on 3 of 8 runs because `stable_bands` treated two EMPTY scans agreeing with each other as settled -- FIXED 2026-08-27
items.source: noticed 2026-08-26 while measuring the dead-session guard: the first shipped-profile run of the day reported 37 PASS / 3 NOT_ESTABLISHED where the handoff recorded 38 / 2, and the extra abstention was this arm
items.note: EIGHT RUNS, SAME MACHINE, SAME PROFILE (e2-editor-v8), SAME HOUR: PASS on five and NOT_ESTABLISHED on three, with `heightWhenOpened: 2007` on all eight and `heightAfterTheEdit: null` on the three that abstained. Not a drift over the hour either -- the abstentions are runs 1, 6 and 8. So the arm did not get past its own precondition -- `if bands and grew['state'] == 'ready'` -- and since `state` was `ready` in the record on both, what came back empty was the BAND SCAN, on a two-page document on the core whose margins are transparent. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE ARM: `tools/check_usable_editor.py` reconciles the `edit-a-real-length-document` row against this check, so a run that happens to abstain here cannot be cited as acceptance evidence -- measured 2026-08-26, the same report that is otherwise green fails the checklist on this one row. An acceptance gate that passes or fails by coin flip teaches its readers to re-run until it is green, which is the habit every part of this net is built to prevent. DONE ALREADY (2026-08-26): the arm now records `bandsBeforeTheEdit`, `scanWidth` and `stateBeforeTheEdit`, so the NEXT occurrence says which precondition failed instead of stopping at `heightWhenOpened`. That is an instrument fix and it is not this item. WHAT IS OWED: why the scan comes back empty here. Candidates, none measured -- the tile for a two-page document may not have been painted when `stable_bands` ran (it has its own retry, and `open_long_document` waits on the doc name rather than on ink); or the aim is at the LAST band and a long document's last line may fall outside the scanned region. Do not fix by widening the retry until the record says which. FIRST READING FROM THE NEW FIELDS, 2026-08-27 (acceptance run for finding 084's fix, shipped profile, shell v43): `bandsBeforeTheEdit: 0`, `scanWidth: 725`, `stateBeforeTheEdit: "ready"`. So it IS the band scan and not the state, which the old record could not have said -- and the scan came back with ZERO bands, not a small number, on a full-width scan of a document the session already called ready. That rules out 'the scan found too few bands to compare' and leaves 'there was no ink on the canvas when it looked'. The next question is unchanged and is now a narrower one: whether the tiles for that document had been painted at the moment of the scan, which is a question about when the arm looks rather than about what it looks for. ANSWERED AND FIXED 2026-08-27. The cause is in the instrument, not the product. `stable_bands()` waited for the scan's shape to REPEAT before trusting it -- written 2026-08-19 after the same page reported 11 bands and then 9, a repaint caught in flight -- and two EMPTY scans agree with each other. A canvas that had not painted yet satisfied the repeat test after one 0.5 s sleep, so the function returned 'settled, zero bands' half a second after the document opened. 'The page has settled with no ink on it' and 'nothing has been drawn yet' were the same answer to that test, which is this tree's own recurring shape: nothing-happened and the-mechanism-never-ran look alike and both look green. THE NEW FIELDS ARE WHAT MADE IT FINDABLE: two more abstentions on 2026-08-27 (acceptance runs for finding 084's fix, shipped profile, shell v43) both recorded `bandsBeforeTheEdit: 0`, `scanWidth: 725`, `stateBeforeTheEdit: ready` -- so the state was fine and the SCAN was empty, which the old record could not have said. THE FIX: an empty shape no longer ends the wait, it uses the whole budget, and the scan records how it finished (`stableBecause: repeated` vs `exhausted`) so the two stay distinguishable afterwards. THE NUMBER THAT PROVES IT WAS THE CAUSE: three runs after the fix, `scanSettledAfterTries: 4` in all three -- ink appears on the FOURTH scan, and the old rule returned at try 2. The canvas really was blank for the first second; the instrument stopped looking before it was painted. All three runs: the arm PASSED with 2 bands, `heightAfterTheEdit: 3002` against `heightWhenOpened: 2007`, and `tools/check_usable_editor.py` reconciles the checklist `ok: true` in all three -- which the two abstaining runs could not do. COST, MEASURED: arms that deliberately expect a blank canvas now spend the full budget before saying so, and a canvas blank for six seconds is a stronger statement than one blank for one; run duration to the last check went 361.4 s -> 364.7 s. NOT SETTLED: why a two-page document takes more than a second to paint on this core. That is a separate question and this only says the instrument was reading before it happened. Evidence: findings/evidence/queue-canvas-grew-arm-abstains-intermittently/.

items.title: finding 084: the page's editorState had TWO writers and only one guard -- the drain's stale read overwrote the announcement that had already delivered the caret; ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED 2026-08-27, no engine change and no link
items.source: the first readings `caret-follows-the-text-you-type` has ever had on this lineage, 2026-08-26, three runs of e2-editor-v10 -- finding 082's fix is what let the runs reach it
items.note:
ONE RUN IN THREE, AND THE OTHER TWO PASSED -- so it is INTERMITTENT, which is the first thing to know about it and the reason it is a queue item rather than a finding. The failing round: `caret-follows-the-text-you-type` on `e2-editor-v10`, chrome:
  round 0  left 163 -> 163   revisionAdvanced: true   moved: FALSE
  round 1  left 163 -> 393   revisionAdvanced: true   moved: true
  round 2  left 393 -> 509   revisionAdvanced: true   moved: true
The text reached the document all three times, so this is not a lost commit: it is the caret position, read from `#sink`, not following the first one. Rounds 2 and 3 are ordinary. `sinkTracksTheCaret: true` in the same record, so the sink is where finding 069 pinned it. WHY IT IS NEW RATHER THAN A REGRESSION: this check had NEVER RUN on the accessibility lineage. Every previous run died at check 17 (finding 082), and before that finding 075's band scan made the earlier arms abstain. So 'it used to pass here' is a sentence nobody can say, and the honest reading is 'first look'. MEASURED 2 of 6 on 2026-08-26 -- `e2-editor-v10` rounds 1/2/3 FAIL/PASS/PASS and `e2-editor-v11` rounds 1/2/3 PASS/FAIL/PASS. AND THE FAILING RUNS ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO EACH OTHER: left 163 -> 163, then 163 -> 393, then 393 -> 509, the same three numbers both times. So it is not noise in the measurement -- it is a deterministic event that fires intermittently, which is a different thing and a better lead. WHAT IS OWED BEFORE IT IS A FINDING: more runs, because 1 of 3 is a rate nobody has bounded. This tree's own rule is that an intermittent defect measured once gives a confident and wrong answer, and one round out of three inside one check is exactly the shape that has fooled it before. Then the same check on `e2-editor-v8`, which passes there, to say whether this is the a11y core or the arm. SHAPE TO SUSPECT, NOT TO INDICT: it is the FIRST read after a caret placement, which is the family findings 048, 051 and 068 all sat in. Do not write that down as the cause until something measures it. CHARACTERISED 2026-08-26 AND FILED AS FINDING 084, and the characterisation refuted my own first reading. From the geometry alone -- nineteen runs all ending at the same position, the failing ones missing one step and then moving twice as far -- I concluded the harness had READ TOO EARLY: the arm waited for the revision and then slept a fixed 1.2 s, which is exactly the wall-clock shape removed from the abort arm the same morning, and this check's own comment records that the defect it covers was originally a race. SO THE SLEEP BECAME A POLL on the check's own predicate, with an 8 s deadline and the wait recorded per commit -- and it could not mask the defect, because nothing is typed while it waits, which is the question to ask before replacing any sleep. IT IS STILL RED, and now it has a number: `settledAfterMs` is 0 or 1 when it works and 8013 -- the deadline -- when it does not. Nothing in between. That is not latency, it is a DROPPED UPDATE, and the caret catches up only when the NEXT commit arrives. 3 of 27 commits on the a11y lineage; 0 of 42 on the product core. THE HARNESS HALF IS DONE (the poll, and the number). THE PRODUCT HALF IS OPEN and this item stays `absent` for it. Next question, and it is one measurement: record the ENGINE's caret state beside `#sink` in the same round, which separates 'the cursor callback never arrived' from 'it arrived and the page did not use it'. Do not name a layer before that -- two build differences, one measurement. ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-27, and the prediction written before the runs held including the mechanism and the signature it named. The page's `snapshot.editorState.caret` has TWO writers: the engine's `editor-state` announcement, handled in editor-shell-v2/narrow-editor-v2-session.js:171-173, which REFUSES to write unless `sourceSequence` advances (finding 068 added that guard, and its comment says why -- 'a slow event could land after a fresher read and move the caret backwards'); and the drain's own `editor.getState()` in editor-shell/editor-session.js:301-311, which has NO such guard and writes whatever its read returned. The symmetric case -- a slow READ landing after a fresher EVENT -- is this defect. Every dropped commit shows the same signature in the page's own belief log: sourceSequence goes BACKWARDS while revision goes forwards in the same row, which identifies the writer because only the drain writes revision and editorState together. The `applied` log shows the sink moved to the new caret and then moved back, so the page drew it correctly for one frame. 10 of 10 dropped commits carry the signature; in all ten the FIRST engine probe -- 52-54 ms after the sink was seen not to move -- already held the new caret, so the engine was never behind. THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN LESSON, and it is the reason the numbers moved: the first version probed the engine BEFORE every commit, which is a real engine command, and under it 24 of 24 commits followed the caret; with the identical configuration and no probe on a passing commit, 10 of 48 dropped (Fisher exact p = 0.012). The first version of the instrument suppressed the defect it was built to measure, and `--caret-engine-probe stalled` is now the default. The layer conclusion does not rest on the probe: `caretBelieved` is a log of what the PAGE was handed, with no engine command involved. SHIPPED PROFILE, same instrument: 24 of 24 passed, and the reason is in the same column -- the shipped core advances sourceSequence by ONE per commit and the accessibility core by TWO, so on the shipped core the caret-bearing announcement is the last thing in a commit, after the drain has written, and there is nothing left to overwrite it. That is a RATE, not immunity: the defective code is shared JavaScript and ships today. STILL `absent` and still unfixed. The remedy is a sourceSequence guard on the drain's write, and its natural home -- EditorSession._drain() -- is in a file bound to E1-C's verdict (check_e1_c_bundle_intact.py, shell bundle 187706b2...), which is the same wall finding 068 hit and why 068's remedy lives in a subclass override. Whether the same trick reaches this write is a design question and is not answered by this measurement. Evidence: findings/evidence/queue-a11y-caret-does-not-move-on-the-first-commit/ -- PREDICTION (written before), METHOD, RESULT, and eight reports. FIXED 2026-08-27, shell generation v43 (7e99d3a3...), no engine change, no link, and no profile repackage -- one file in editor-shell-v2 is the whole remedy, which is cheaper than 083's because the worker is untouched. `NarrowEditorV2Session` now wraps its state machine's `update` and refuses the `editorState` field of any patch whose `sourceSequence` went BACKWARDS, letting the rest of the patch through. Four design decisions, each with a test and each with a mutation that turns that test red: it wraps `update` and NOT `transition`, because a reopen builds a fresh engine whose counter starts near zero and that is a LEGITIMATE move backwards; it drops the whole `editorState` rather than merging field by field, because both sides are consistent snapshots of one moment and a per-field merge assembles a state that never existed (every field the page reads -- caret, selection, format, caretParagraph, documentOutline -- is carried by both); a write with NO sourceSequence is not second-guessed, because not-knowing is a different claim from going backwards; and an EQUAL sequence is allowed, because the drain's read answered at the sequence the announcement carried is the same moment. Mutations run 2026-08-27: guard removed (6 tests red), installed but never stripping (2 red), also refusing equal (1 red), dropping the whole patch (1 red). A fifth test pins that `editor-shell/editor-session.js` assigns `this.state` exactly ONCE -- a base class that ever replaced the machine would silently drop the wrapper while every other test stayed green. MEASURED, and the acceptance condition was written before the runs: green is not enough, the GUARD MUST HAVE FIRED, or a clean run has only shown that the race was not lost. Three runs on e2-editor-v11, 36 commits: 0 dropped (against 10 of 48 before), `settledAfterMs` now only 0 or 1 with the 8013 ms mode gone entirely, and the guard refused 2, 10 and 7 stale writes per run -- 12 of them inside a typing round, so the race was still being lost and was caught every time. The rest fired OUTSIDE the caret arm, so this was never only about typing. Shipped profile with the fix: 38 PASS / 2 NOT_ESTABLISHED, ok true, and the guard fired ZERO times -- consistent with that core advancing sourceSequence by one per commit, and it means the fix cannot regress what it never touches. The counter is read through `window.__ppStaleWrites`, installed by --caret-source-diagnostic. CHARACTERISED 2026-08-27 (second measurement, asked for by adjudication). The extra announcement on the accessibility core has a name and it is read from the engine's own dispatch rather than inferred: `LOK_CALLBACK_A11Y_FOCUS_CHANGED` -> `editorSource = "a11y-paragraph-changed"` (src/probe_engine.cpp:2433). Per commit: the shipped core emits ONE announcement (`visible-cursor`) on 12 of 12 commits; the accessibility core emits TWO (`a11y-paragraph-changed` then `visible-cursor`) on 24 of 24 -- deterministically one extra, never three and never one. AND THE EXTRA ONE CARRIES A CARET OF ITS OWN, the STALE one: the accessibility paragraph callback fires before the cursor has moved, so a commit produces two announcements that both claim to describe the caret and the drain's read can be answered against either. That is the window. The adjudication warned against attributing the doubling to 'a11y' because the core changed two variables at once (writer+calc AND accessibility); that warning is honoured -- this is the accessibility focus callback by construction, and nothing here measures or claims anything about calc. Post-fix re-measured at MORE than the pre-fix sample: 60 commits on v11 (pre-fix was 48), 0 dropped, with the guard refusing 28 stale writes -- the race is still lost and caught every time. 24 commits on the shipped profile, 0 dropped, guard fired 0 times, which one-announcement-per-commit predicts. The guard is now proven ORDER-INDEPENDENT rather than currently winning: the invariant 'after any interleaving the snapshot holds the highest sourceSequence written' is driven over all 24 permutations of four arrivals, plus duplicates in every position, plus a hostile stream, plus the two-announcements-per-commit shape in all three orders. Mutations: guard removed 6 red, never-stripping 2 red, `>` 7 red, `<=` 2 red.

items.checkNote: Five, and the second one is the load-bearing one: `next < current` is the guard's whole semantics, and both directions of getting it wrong are defects -- `<=` refuses a write that is not stale, `>` inverts it. The third pins the REOPEN test specifically, because that is the case where the guard must NOT fire and the one a later simplification would delete first: a fresh engine's sequence starts near zero, and a guard that refused it would leave the new caret unreachable forever. The fourth pins the harness's record of how many stale writes were refused -- without it a run can go green having never exercised the guard at all, which is the difference between 'the fix works' and 'the race was not lost this time'. items.title: on the accessibility core a blank paragraph selects NOTHING, the barrier calls that a stall, and the disposition attached to a stall is a rollback
items.source: the only consistent red left on the a11y lineage once finding 082 was fixed, 2026-08-26; measured on both cores the same day
items.note: FINDING 083, filed and fixed the same day. `.uno:SelectText` on the blank paragraph selects nothing on the accessibility core, so `maybeAdvanceFormatBarrierSelection` -- which needs the select command's own result AND non-empty rectangles -- never advances, the barrier waits out 5000 ms and reports `stage-deadline:awaiting-selection`, whose disposition is `rollback`. The user pressing the bullet button on a blank line was told to discard every edit since the last checkpoint, on a session that may have none, over a bullet that had applied. MEASURED ON BOTH CORES, same recipe and same cell: v8 reaches `awaiting-restore` with `selectionType: 1` and a two-paragraph readback (finding 046's overshoot) and gets `review`; v10 stops at `awaiting-selection` with `selectionType: -1` and zero bytes read. The ACTION is identical on both (`success: false, wasModified: true`, finding 020's shape). WHY THE CORES DIFFER IS NOT ESTABLISHED and no layer is named: two build differences, one measurement (findings 040 and 048's rule), and it is not even obvious which behaviour is right -- not overshooting into the neighbour is arguably the better one. FIXED WITHOUT TOUCHING THE ENGINE OR TAKING A LINK. The disposition already lives in JavaScript. Three parts: the worker forwards `selectionResultSeen` (the engine always sent it; the allowlist dropped it, and without it nobody can tell 'the engine never answered' from 'it answered and nothing was selected'); the client adds a branch narrowed on FOUR conditions, three of which have mutations that turn the test red; and the page gets its OWN SENTENCE for this shape, because reaching `review` with the multi-block explanation would tell the user the check 'covered more than one paragraph' about a paragraph where nothing was selected -- finding 061's shape, already filed once. THE ACCEPTANCE CONDITION MOVED WITH THE PRESCRIPTION, deliberately and with the reason written in: `bulleting-a-blank-line-does-not-demand-a-rollback` pinned the multi-block sentence and would have gone red on a product that had just been fixed. It now accepts either sentence, still pins the shared promise (`不是你要的就按「復原」`), still refuses `請回到檢查點`, and RECORDS WHICH sentence it saw -- so the two cores' different routes to `review` stay visible instead of being flattened. SHELL GENERATION v42, frozen ONCE after both shell edits -- the first freeze was premature (the page half was still to come) and was withdrawn rather than forced over. MEASURED on `e2-editor-v11`, which is v10's artifact repackaged (same wasm, same loader, only `workerSha256` moves; no link): the check PASSES, the toast carries the new sentence, and the run is 37 PASS / 3 NOT_ESTABLISHED, `ok: true` -- THE FIRST CLEAN PRODUCT PATH THE ACCESSIBILITY LINEAGE HAS EVER PRODUCED. DECLARED COST: `notice-action-recovers-the-session` goes back to NOT_ESTABLISHED on this lineage, because the cell no longer blocks the queue. Same trade as 2026-08-17 on the product core, and `finish()`'s recovery pairing caught it in the same run.
items.checkNote: Four, one per layer the fix crosses, because any one of them alone is inert: the worker field without the client branch changes nothing, the client branch without the field can never fire, and both without the page's sentence give the user `review` with a reason that is false about their document. The fourth pins the HARNESS's record of which sentence it saw -- without it the check would go green on either core and stop being able to show that they reach `review` by different routes.

items.title: a new shell generation inherits its exclusions from the newest LISTED manifest, not the newest EXISTING one, and nothing goes red when those differ -- OPEN
items.source: found 2026-09-03 by the revert rehearsal that included step 3 (findings/evidence/queue-v12-cutover-revert/RESULT-2026-09-03-step-3-rehearsed.md); the freeze of v44 reported exclusionsInheritedFrom = v40
items.note:
`FROZEN_MANIFESTS` in tools/build_e2_c_shell_bundle.py ends at v40 while v41, v42 and v43 exist in e2/. Adding a generation to that tuple is a MANUAL step and it has lagged three generations. When a freeze passes no --exclude the builder walks that tuple in reverse for exclusions to inherit, so it inherits from the newest LISTED manifest rather than the newest EXISTING one.

MEASURED 2026-09-03: no difference for this cutover. v40, v41, v42 and v43 carry the same three exclusions item for item (sdk/sdk-worker.js, reader-shell/reader-session.js, reader-shell/state-machine.js), so v44 came out identical either way. That is luck rather than mechanism: had any of the three changed an exclusion, v44 would have silently inherited v40's and NOTHING WOULD HAVE GONE RED. The builder reports `exclusionsInheritedFrom` honestly and no check reads it.

The builder's own comment anticipated the manual step being missed -- "Adding it to FROZEN_MANIFESTS is a manual step, so 'not yet listed there' cannot be what protects it" -- and the guard it then wrote protects against OVERWRITING a generation, not against INHERITING from a stale one. A guard written for one half of a hazard is a reminder that the other half was considered and not covered.

NOT FIXED MID-GATE, deliberately: changing the builder while the cutover gate is running is an instrument change the gate cannot absorb, and the measured outcome for this cutover is unaffected. Two candidate fixes, both post-cutover: catch FROZEN_MANIFESTS up to v43 (mechanical, preserves the tuple's meaning as the record of what has been frozen), or make the inheritance walk use the newest EXISTING generation file (structural, and removes the manual step from the hazard path). Either way the acceptance condition is fixed now: a freeze whose ancestor is not the immediately preceding generation must be REFUSED or reported as a problem, not merely recorded in a field nobody reads.
items.checkNote: The first two together ARE the defect: the tuple's last entry is v40 and v43 exists on disk. When the item is closed by catching the tuple up, the first check stops being the last entry and this pair must be rewritten to state whatever the fix makes true -- with the reason, per the rule that an acceptance condition may be changed but never silently.

items.title: the accessibility projection this core exists for does not extend to Calc views: `no accessibility broadcaster?` on every spreadsheet open -- OPEN
items.source: measured 2026-09-03 by the ODS milestone's decisive measurement (findings/evidence/m4-ods/RESULT-W2-the-decisive-measurement.md)
items.note:
Every spreadsheet opened on e2-editor-v12 logs, three times, immediately after `open.query-metadata` -- which is where refreshEditorAccessibility() calls setAccessibilityState(view, true):

  warn:legacy.osl:sc/source/ui/view/tabvwshh.cxx:237: no accessibility broadcaster?

No ODT case logs it. The document still opens, the view initialises and the tile paints, so this does NOT wedge -- that half was the registered unknown and it is now answered.

THE OTHER HALF IS THE POINT. A Calc view in this build has no accessibility broadcaster, so the document projection that justifies this core -- the thing gate condition 4a measures and the whole v12 cutover is being paid for -- DOES NOT EXTEND TO SPREADSHEETS as it stands. An ODS viewer built on this core would be as inaccessible as the product is today.

Not a reason to stop the ODS milestone: the owner asked for READING ODS and route B is a read-only viewer. It is a reason that milestone may never be described as 'accessible spreadsheet reading' anywhere, and a reason to size the work before anyone assumes it rides along with the Writer projection.

Nothing measured yet about WHY: whether the broadcaster is absent because ScTabViewShell does not create one under --disable-gui, or because the accessibility factory is stripped for Calc, or because the call arrives before the view is ready. That question is the first work item if this is ever taken up, and guessing between the three is what this note exists to prevent.
items.checkNote: The first check pins the call site the warning comes from, so a rename or removal reddens this item rather than silently orphaning it. It does NOT assert the defect is present -- that is what the banked measurement is for; a check that tried to assert it would need a browser run per queue pass.

items.title: run_e2_c_d4.py polls one namespace and the heap page publishes to another, so a page that finished in 9 s is reported as a 40-minute product failure -- OPEN
items.source: measured 2026-09-03 while taking the ODS milestone's memory baseline (findings/evidence/m4-ods/RESULT-W1-v12-boot-baseline.md)
items.note:
tools/run_e2_c_d4.py polls `globalThis.<namespace>` with --namespace defaulting to `__e2c_d4`. web/e2-c-d4-heap-app.js publishes to `globalThis.__e2c_d4_heap` (and to `__probe_metrics`). Run the heap page without the flag and the runner waits out its full 2400 s timeout and writes:

  "complete": false, "cycles": 0, "samples": 0,
  "error": {"code": "RUNNER_TIMEOUT", "message": "page never completed"}

while the page's OWN log, written beside it in the same directory, says `{"complete":true,"cycles":3}` with the last cycle ending at 8,830 ms.

This is the worst class of instrument error this tree files: it does not merely fail to measure, it REPORTS A PRODUCT FAILURE THAT DID NOT HAPPEN, and it does so with a timeout long enough to look like a real investigation. A reader taking RUNNER_TIMEOUT at face value would open a memory investigation into a core that boots in two seconds.

The fix is not to pass the flag. It is for the runner to say WHICH namespace it polled and what else it found -- `__probe_metrics` is right there and would have named the mismatch immediately. ACCEPTANCE CONDITION, fixed now: a run that times out must report the namespace it polled, and must state whether any sibling metrics object exists on the page; a timeout that cannot distinguish 'the page never finished' from 'I was looking in the wrong place' is not a measurement.
items.checkNote: The two together ARE the defect: the runner interpolates a namespace and the heap page publishes under a different one. When the item is closed the pair must be rewritten to state what the fix made true, with the reason.

blocksRelinkSemantics: An item with blocksRelink true must be AS-DECLARED **and**, if it is declared absent, it is still outstanding work -- so P1 is not complete while it is open. Two items are deliberately false: the WASM heap field was withdrawn after measurement (2026-08-16), and the search-after-reopen wedge is an observation the product does not take today. Without this field the checker would report 'P1 complete' whenever every finished item was finished, which is the exact shape of a check that agrees with whatever it is shown.
externalAdjudication2026_08_16: fable, called as a subagent, refuted the premise that the two remaining blockers cannot be measured before the relink. Verified independently, all three claims: (1) tools/build_e2_discovery_profile.py COPIES the wasm (shutil.copy2, --wasm is an input), so a diagnostic profile can be packaged around the frozen 572035ac bytes -- no engine build, same engine; (2) the frozen wasm already serialises "readback":{"parsed": / "blockCount": / "itemCount": / "html":" and "containment":{"checked": (one occurrence each; "preBlocksObserved": zero, correct -- that is today's unlinked change); (3) all six worker patch anchors match exactly once in the FROZEN dist worker. Consequence: 3b's criterion and the containment ordering are both measurable now, for the price of a Python repackage plus browser rounds. Linking before that measurement would risk a v4, which costs the whole E2-B rerun plus E2-C D0-D5 again.

linkDecision.why: `p1Complete: True` means nothing is BLOCKING the link; it does not mean the link should happen now. Held deliberately so the newly characterised engine defect (queue-selecttext-overshoots-empty-paragraph) has a chance to ride along: it is an engine fix, so it can only ship through a link, and linking today would make it cost a second one.
